chunks: And as for what Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:

"The divorce that Allah loves, and which the jurist (al-faqih) pronounces, and he is the fair one between the woman and the man, is that he divorces her during the period of purity, with the testimony of two witnesses, and with intention from the heart. Then he leaves her until three menstrual periods (quru') pass. When she sees blood in the first drop of the third period, which is the last of the periods (because the periods are the periods of purity), then she is definitively divorced from him, and she has authority over herself. If she wishes, she may marry, and she becomes permissible to him without a husband [in between]. If he does this with her a hundred times, he nullifies what came before, and she becomes permissible to him without a husband. And if he revokes her before she gains authority over herself, then divorces her three times, revoking and divorcing each time, she does not become permissible to him except through another husband."

This narration is the most probable of all the preceding narrations because it does not admit any of what we said, due to its explicit nature and freedom from various possibilities. However, its chain of transmission is Abdullah ibn Bukayr, and we have previously presented from the reports that he said when asked about this matter: 'This is what Allah granted him of opinion (ra'y).'

If he had heard that from Zurarah, he would have said when al-Husayn ibn Hashim and others asked him about it, and asked him if he had anything regarding it, he would have said: 'Yes, the narration of Zurarah,' and would not have said: 'Yes, the narration of Rifah.' Until the questioner said to him: 'Indeed, the narration of Rifah includes that if there is a husband between them...' He said: 'That is what Allah the Exalted granted him of opinion.'

So he shifted from saying that this is in the narration of Rifah to saying: 'The husband and the non-husband are the same to me.' When the questioner pressed him, he said: 'This is what Allah granted him of opinion.' And since this is its form, it is permissible that he attributed that to the narration of Zurarah to support the school of thought he had previously issued fatwa according to.

And that when he saw that his companions did not accept what he said by his own opinion, he attributed it to the one who narrated it from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). And Abdullah ibn Bukayr is not infallible, so this is permissible for him. Rather, what occurred from him was shifting from the belief in the school of truth to the belief in the school of al-Fatah, which is known from his school.
And the error in that is greater than attributing an erroneous fatwa to someone who believes in its correctness due to affection for some of the Imams (peace be upon them).
And if the matter is as we said, then this narration does not contradict what we presented.

If it is said: Do you not claim that the reports you narrated regarding one who is not permissible to him 'until she marries another husband' indicate the opposite of what you mentioned, that whoever divorces his wife three divorces, the divorce of the Sunnah, is not permissible to him 'until she marries another husband', because it includes mentioning the details of the divorce of the waiting period, and does not include mentioning the divorce of the Sunnah in any way?

It is said to him: There is nothing in those hadiths that contradicts what we presented, because what is in them is mentioning the ruling of the divorce of the waiting period, and that whoever divorces his wife three divorces, the divorce of the waiting period, is not permissible to him 'until she marries another husband'. And it is not explicit in them that whoever divorces his wife three divorces for the Sunnah, what is his ruling, except from the aspect of the implication of the wording (dalil al-khitab).
And it is permissible to abandon the implication of the wording for an implication, which is what we presented from the reports.
As for what he mentioned, may Allah have mercy on him, from his saying that he says: 'If he intends divorce, so-and-so is divorced, or she is divorced,' and points to her, he narrated that.

key_terms.رَزَقَهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الرَّأْيِ: What Allah granted him of opinion/judgment

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid divorce according to the narration of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and how is the chain of transmission analyzed?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines the procedural requirements for *Talaq al-Sunnah* (divorce according to the Sunnah), emphasizing divorce during purity (*istiqbal al-tuhr*) with two witnesses and a waiting period of three menstrual cycles (*quru'*). The text critically analyzes the narrator Abdullah ibn Bukayr, suggesting he may have attributed this ruling to Zurarah to support his own juristic opinion (*ra'y*) regarding the nature of the divorce, highlighting the Shia scholarly method of evaluating narrator credibility and potential bias in legal transmission.
